comparison_policy.aggregate_tier_note: The validator vocabulary offers BYTE_IDENTICAL, BYTE_IDENTICAL_CANONICAL_PIXEL_DIGEST and CANONICAL_PIXEL_HAMMING_WITHIN_THRESHOLD. 17 of 18 pairs are raw PNG byte-identical and the remaining pair is canonical-digest byte-identical at canonical Hamming 0, so the aggregate is BYTE_IDENTICAL_CANONICAL_PIXEL_DIGEST. The Hamming tier is NOT used: its max would be 0, which is a digest identity, not a tolerance.

canonical16_technique.name: SRC047_CANONICAL16
canonical16_technique.digest: sha256 of the 1024-byte RGBA buffer; equality is exact, a normalization not a tolerance

pair_tiers.note: CANONICAL_PIXEL_DIGEST here means the 16x16 canonical digest is byte-identical (canonical Hamming 0 of 1024 bytes) while the raw PNG bytes differ. This is the CENTRAL-decided tier for the single differing pair, per #589 comment 5556645775.

comparison_policy.screenshot_pixel_tolerance: REMOVED (the raw pixel measurement is retained only as a recording instrument for the one raw-differing pair; it never decides equality)

non_byte_identical_pair.computed_style_result: EQUAL (opacity, h1 fontSize, footer backgroundColor all deep-equal)

non_byte_identical_pair.canonical_digest_result: BYTE_IDENTICAL (16x16 canonical pixel digest sha256 equal, Hamming 0 of 1024 bytes)
non_byte_identical_pair.assessment: ANTIALIASING_NOISE_ONLY: 14 pixels on one footer text row, maximum per-channel delta 1/255 (LSB rounding). No layout, text, color, geometry or structural difference. Both PNGs are committed and retained for CENTRAL review; neither was discarded, averaged or repaired.

state_and_interaction_comparison.method: assert.deepStrictEqual on the full captured state object and the interaction record for every matched state on both surfaces (strict, no epsilon)

footer in-view flag and computed background color
state_and_interaction_comparison.viewport_normalization: Rects rounded to 3 decimals and scroll progress to 6 decimals inside the shared S2 driver, identically for both surfaces. No additional normalization was applied for parity.
